topLevel.why: X gives each story, the introduction and the agent's essay its own part, and every boundary falls where a new story begins. Y welds several stories into themed bundles, and its 'Cognitive Radio' part actually starts at Power Punctuation, so Liberation Spectrum ends up inside 'Human Readable'.

gists.why: Both trees give detailed gists that mostly agree. X's gist fits the customs-line passage exactly, where Y's describes the later interrogation, while Y fits the spam-response passage better. Elsewhere they are roughly even.

weldedParts.why: Welds 'The Right Book' and 'Other People's Money', two separate stories.
Runs from block 805 to 1521, absorbing the whole of 'Liberation Spectrum' (block 1264 onward).
Its title and gist claim to cover 'Liberation Spectrum' and 'Power Punctuation!', but it starts at Power Punctuation, so it misnames and mixes divisions.
Welds 'Visit the Sins', 'Constitutional Crisis' and 'Pester Power'.

weldedParts.part: Vats, AIs, and the Business of Writing
weldedParts.why: Welds 'Chicken Little', 'Epoch' and Russell Galen's essay 'I'm Only In It For the Money'.
Folds the front matter (title, contents, dedication, publication history) into the introduction.

overall.why: X's top level maps one-to-one onto the book's stories with correct boundaries, while Y's bundles are misaligned and blur the divisions. X's gists are also at least as good as Y's.
